Beans have gotten cheaper. At that news, your wallet pumps its fist. In your mind, the price of your usual cup has already come down, too. But the price tag in a shop may not change right away. When you see a price tag that makes you want to say, haven't you heard the news? It seems there is a time lag. The price measure reported by the International Coffee Organization fell 8.7% from the previous month. The reason, it said, was that more beans harvested in Brazil had entered the market and a good supply was expected to continue. The U.S. Department of Agriculture said that earlier high prices came from several factors happening at once: bad weather in Brazil and Vietnam, fewer beans available for sale, and strong demand.

Meanwhile, U.S. consumer price data showed that the price of coffee was 6.1% higher than in the same month a year earlier. It may leave you wondering, did prices go down or up? But the data covers a different month from the bean price measure, and it does not show the price of a cup at a cafe. Hold on before putting the two figures in the ring. So how long does it take for the price of beans to reach a price tag? According to estimates from market insiders and experts interviewed by Reuters, it takes at least about nine months for the price of raw beans to show up in U.S. retail prices. The road to a price tag is quite a long journey. The article says that companies in the U.S. that roast coffee keep raw beans in stock. Roasting and packing the beans also take time. They also often negotiate prices with retailers on a regular basis. The price tag in a shop does not flash to a new price the moment the market moves.

However, the about nine-month figure is an estimate based on interviews. It is not a rule that applies to every company, and it is not a promise that prices will fall in nine months. It is too soon to mark the date on your calendar. And a cup at a cafe comes with costs besides the beans. One cafe operator in Chicago said that the cost of cups and labor, as well as the cost of buying beans, had been behind price increases. Even if bean prices fall, other costs do not always fall along with them. If you are waiting for the price of your usual cup to come down, think not only how much do beans cost now, but also when does the price of the beans reach here. A coffee price tag may have an unseen clock of its own, separate from the latest news about the market.
